title: Profiling through continuous sensor data
description: The wearable device continuously collects heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps, enabling detailed profiling of the user's health patterns, movement behaviors, and location history. This data can be analyzed to link and infer personal characteristics about the individual.
assumptions: Device processes and stores sensor data for analysis

title: Quasi-identifier combination enables identification
description: The combination of GPS position, timestamps, heart rate patterns, and step counts creates a quasi-identifier that can uniquely identify the data subject, even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Multiple sensor data types are combined in processing

title: Collection of sensitive data types
description: GPS position and heart rate data are highly sensitive personal data types. Continuous collection of such data may exceed what is functionally required for basic wearable functionality.
assumptions: Device collects all sensor types continuously

title: Excessive data collection frequency
description: Continuous capture of sensor telemetry means data is processed more frequently than functionally needed for most use cases, creating excessive volume of personal data.
assumptions: Continuous collection without user-configurable intervals

title: Lack of user control over data collection preferences
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding which sensor data types are collected, how frequently, and for what purposes during continuous device operation.
assumptions: Device operates with default settings without granular user controls

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Continuous collection of multiple sensitive data types (GPS, heart rate, step counts) may process more personal data than actually needed for the wearable's core functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: All sensor data is collected regardless of functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific use case and consent mechanisms

title: Unique device identifier enables cross-session linking

assumptions: Device id is unique and persistent across sessions

title: Quasi-identifier combination in transit
description: The combination of GPS traces, timestamps, and exercise session data in the data flow creates a quasi-identifier that can link to a specific individual through pattern analysis.
